section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the soul is adjured to be righteous because the body and animal soul can conceal it, and the oath draws from the soul's root in the Essence of Ein Sof, giving it power.
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "they adjure him: 'Be righteous,'"
that the need to adjure the soul "be righteous,"
even though this
(to be righteous)
is the will of the soul,
is because through its enclothing in the body and the animal soul,
it is possible that the body and the animal soul conceal and hide the soul.
And especially since the root of the G-dly soul is in Tikkun (rectification), and the root of the animal soul is in Tohu (chaos) that preceded Tikkun.
Therefore they adjure the soul: "Be righteous,"
for the concept of the oath is the drawing down of the root of the soul as it is rooted in the Essence of Ein Sof
(above the concept of Tohu and Tikkun),
and through this it can overcome the animal soul.
And this "they adjure him" is also from the term "satisfaction" (sova),
for satisfaction is the giving of power.
And through the oath,
the drawing down of the root of the soul as it is rooted in the Essence of Ein Sof
[which is analogous to the root of the son as it is in the father's brain itself before it is drawn down],
they give power to the soul as it is in revelation above
[which is analogous to the son as he is drawn from the father's brain],
and also to the soul as it is enclothed in the body and animal soul,
to perform its service of turning from evil
("Do not be wicked")
and doing good
("Be righteous").

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies how the oath helps the soul over the body and animal soul, which are not in its domain, by drawing from the level of "By Myself I have sworn" where even they are under the soul's authority.
section.t: e)
Now, the Tzemach Tzedek questions
regarding the statement "they adjure him: 'Be righteous,'"
how does the oath help the soul over the body and animal soul,
since this is something not in its domain,
and surely a person cannot transfer ownership of something not in his possession.
And he explains,
that this [concept] that they adjure him "be righteous" our Sages learned from the verse,
"For to Me every knee shall bend, every tongue shall swear."
"For to Me every knee shall bend" — this is the day of death,
"every tongue shall swear" — this is the day of birth.
And the beginning of this verse is "By Myself I have sworn,"
where "By Myself" refers to Atik
(as above).
And that "every tongue shall swear" comes in continuation of "By Myself I have sworn,"
meaning,
that in the oath with which they adjure him "be righteous," power is drawn from the level of "By Myself I have sworn."
And with this power,
the soul is able to dominate the animal soul.
And it can be said,
that the explanation of how the oath helps the soul over the body and animal soul, which is something not in its domain,
is,
that from the perspective of the level of "By Myself I have sworn,"
even the body and animal soul are in the domain of the soul.
For in the level of revelations,
the soul and the body and animal soul are two separate matters.
For the root of the soul is in Tikkun, and the root of the body and animal soul is in Tohu.
But in Ein Sof, which is above Tohu and Tikkun,
since the original intention in the construction and destruction of Tohu was that the refinement of Tohu
(the root of the body and animal soul)
should be accomplished through Tikkun
(the root of the G-dly soul),
therefore, through the revelation of Ein Sof,
even the body and animal soul become within the domain of the soul,
because the purpose of their very coming into being from the outset is that they be refined through the soul.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the two meanings of "adjure"—as an oath (drawing the soul's root) and as satisfaction (revealing that drawing as power within the soul to overcome and refine the animal soul).
section.t: f)
And it can be said,
that the difference between the two concepts of "they adjure him,"
"adjure" from the term "oath" and "adjure" from the term "satisfaction,"
is,
that "adjure" from the term "oath" is the drawing down of the root of the soul,
and "adjure" from the term "satisfaction" is that this drawing down should be in revelation within the soul as it comes in the drawing down
(including the soul as it is enclothed in the body and animal soul),
analogous to literal satisfaction,
where food satisfies a person.
And this is that "they adjure him" from the term "satisfaction" is the giving of power
(as explained in many places),
for through the drawing down of the oath being in revelation within the soul that is in the body,
it has the power to overcome the animal soul
(as above, section d),
and also to effect its refinement and purification
(as above, section e),
for which purpose it descended below.
And as explained in Tanya,
that the ultimate purpose of the soul's descent below is
(not for the sake of the soul,
but rather)
in order to refine and purify the body and animal soul and its portion in the world.
